key_facts: Primary neoplasms often appear as a discrete soft-tissue mass with enhancement, invasion, or mass effect.
Benign and non-neoplastic entities can mimic tumor, including cysts, abscesses, hematoma, and inflammatory phlegmon.
Determining whether the mass arises from liver, pancreas, kidney, bowel, or retroperitoneum is central to interpretation.
Associated findings such as lymphadenopathy, metastases, vascular encasement, or organ distortion raise concern for malignancy.
CT characterization is limited by contrast phase; multiphase imaging and clinical context may be needed for further evaluation.
